content:
nina: heads up — after applying the TF changes to use ephemeral SA + IRSA for the vectorizer CSI mount, pods can't decrypt secrets. PR: https://git.internal/repo/pull/499

rahul: which cluster/namespace and can you dump the exact CSI error?

nina: staging / ns=vectorizer. CSI log:
```
E0104 08:47:03.112 1 csi.go:198] decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/irsa-svc-role/ci-20240104 not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-1234-ef56
```

sam: ok that STS assumed-role pattern is the IRSA session ARN. Two usual suspects:
- key policy only allows the role principal (iam::123456789012:role/irsa-svc-role) but not the assumed-role/session ARN
- aws_kms_grant exists but was applied before role propagation (cross-module race)

jia: are you relying only on the key policy or do you create an aws_kms_grant? grants are more reliable for short-lived sessions.

nina: we have a key policy that lists the role arn, AND a grant in a separate infra module. sometimes the infra module for grants runs earlier (remote state) and fails to map the role. we don't have explicit depends_on. also CI gives the role name a suffix (ci-20240104) which confused an exact-match policy in one run.

rahul: two fixes i've used:
1) make the key policy accept the assumed-role pattern: e.g. "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/irsa-svc-role/*" so session ARNs match. keep it scoped by account+role to avoid opening the key.
2) create an aws_kms_grant that references the role ARN (or module output) so TF orders the grant after the role. example we used:
```
resource "aws_kms_grant" "svc_kms_grant" {
  name               = "svc-kms-grant-${var.env}"
  key_id             = aws_kms_key.app_key.key_id
  grantee_principal  = try(module.irsa.role_arn, aws_iam_role.irsa.arn)
  operations         = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey*"]
  depends_on         = [module.irsa] // ensure role/module is ready when grant created
}
```
This avoids matching the session ARN directly in the key policy and handles CI suffixes.

sam: add on: if the key is in another account you also need the proper cross-account principal in the key policy and include aws:SourceAccount conditions. also note that grants are scoped to a key id — if you rotate or recreate the key you need to re-run the grant.

nina: perfect. i'll update the key policy to allow the assumed-role/* pattern and move the grant into the same module (or add a depends_on referencing module.irsa) and re-run. will post the CI plan. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: terraform-plan (module/irsa) finished — plan shows aws_kms_grant will be added (run 500).
